title: Dynamic Embedding Slipstream Provisioner: predictive reservoir + burst smoothing
creator: Aisha Kapoor
description: Goal: Implement a lightweight, tenant-aware provisioning controller (Slipstream Provisioner) that reduces p99 tail and cost volatility for high-variance embedding workloads. The controller combines short-term predictive bumps, time-windowed reservoir tokens, and burst smoothing to: 1) prevent headlong queue growth during sudden tenant spikes, 2) avoid over-provisioning steady-state by reclaiming unused headroom, and 3) respect tenant rate limits and overall cluster capacity budgets.
acceptance_criteria: 1) New provisioner can be toggled per-tenant via Console (on/off) and defaults to off for current clusters. 2) Demonstrated p99 embedding latency reduction >= 15% on spike workload in benchmark harness compared to current autoscaler baseline. 3) No increase in cluster GPU utilization >5% for steady traffic patterns. 4) Graceful fallback path to existing autoscaler if metrics stream is unavailable. 5) End-to-end integration tests and a canary rollout plan documented.
implementation_plan: Phase 1: Prototype slipstream controller in staging that consumes ingress rate, queue depth, and recent service-time histograms. Phase 2: Add short-horizon predictor (exponential smoothing + anomaly detector) that proposes temporary headroom reservations for 30-120s windows. Phase 3: Implement reservoir token buckets per-tenant with prioritized draining and backpressure signals to router. Phase 4: Integrate with admission controller to preemptively route to fallbacks when headroom exhausted. Phase 5: Metrics/telemetry and controlled canary rollout. Phase 6: Post-rollout monitoring and iterative tuning.
telemetry_and_metrics: Required signals: per-tenant qps, queue_length, p50/p95/p99 latency, GPU_utilization_by_pool, token_reservoir_levels, admission_denials, rate_limit_trips. Dashboards to add: Slipstream Overview, Canary vs Baseline comparison, Per-tenant warm-pool heatmap. Alerts: p99 latency > baseline *1.2 for 5m; admission_denials > 0.5% over 10m for canary tenants.
rollout_plan: 1) Internal staging test with synthetic spikes (1x, 5x, 10x) on small cluster. 2) Canary: enable for 3 low-risk tenants for 24h with close monitoring. 3) Expand to 20 tenants across regions for 72h. 4) Full rollout opt-in via Console toggle. 5) Automatic rollback if alert triggers. Communicate to customer success and support before canary start.
risks_and_mitigations: Risk: Predictor overestimates spikes and causes wasted reserved GPUs. Mitigation: cap transient reservations and prefer short windows with fast reclaim. Risk: Interaction with existing dedicated reserved pools. Mitigation: add explicit compatibility rules and tagging so slipstream won't touch dedicated-only pools. Risk: Telemetry outages causing controller instability. Mitigation: fail closed to legacy autoscaler and add synthetic heartbeat signals.
notes: Design trade-offs considered: heavy ML forecasting vs lightweight smoothing; we chose exponential smoothing + thresholded anomaly detector to avoid model drift and maintain low ops overhead. Avoided coupling with kernel selection logic to keep rollout low-risk. We'll evaluate adding a simple ML forecaster in Q3 if stable.
